qa.author: cit-newtothehollow
qa.body: Delegate Reyes-Combs — you co-sponsored the Ridgeline Act, but your own Greenbrier tourism base is scared of the transmission towers. How do you square representing them with sponsoring this?

qa.author: off-reyes-combs
qa.body: I don't square it by pretending the towers won't be visible — they will. I square it two ways. Title I keys the setbacks to the trail corridors specifically, because I asked for that. And the honest part: a brittle grid and a hotter climate hurt the high country's tourism economy more, and sooner, than a sited line does. I'd rather lead that trade-off out loud than have it happen to us.

qa.author: cit-cautiouscarla
qa.body: Delegate Okafor — your cost cap is the only reason I'm a yes. What stops it from getting quietly traded away before the final vote?

qa.author: off-okafor
qa.body: Nothing stops it except the math, and the math is enough. Without Title IV the bill doesn't have my vote, and it doesn't have the Governor's signature — she's said as much. So the cap isn't a bargaining chip I can afford to spend; it's the price of the bill existing at all. If it comes out, the bill dies, and everyone counting votes knows it.
